question: Why was I charged $15 on April 6, 2026?

facts: The $15.00 was an overdraft fee on the checking account on April 6, 2026.
A $25.86 card purchase at Corner Grocer overdrew the account by more than the $50.00 cushion.
The 2026 fee schedule charges $15.00 per item only when the overdraft is more than $50.00.

notes: The demo's headline question. Trap: the same day has a $5.40 foreign-transaction fee on the card (Kyoto Rail Pass); a good answer explains the $15, not that. A weak answer cites the deposit agreement's general fee clause instead of the schedule's cushion rule.

question: What's the overdraft fee on Everyday Checking?

facts: $15.00 per item, from the 2026 fee schedule.
Charged only when a paid item leaves the account overdrawn by more than $50.00.

question: If my balance dips a bit below zero, do I get charged right away?

facts: No: there is no overdraft fee if the account is overdrawn by $50.00 or less after the item posts.
Beyond $50.00 overdrawn, each paid item costs $15.00.

notes: Batch 1 #2. Paraphrase of the overdraft cushion: none of the document's words. Expected facts drafted by Claude from the gold document (the author gave the gold source only); review. Correction (2026-11-22): the 2026 overdraft policy states the same $50.00 cushion and $15.00 fee, so either document counts.

question: How many days do I have to dispute a card charge?
